title: Using devices of style and tone (1)

instruction.text: Fill in the gaps to complete the given devices of style and tone.

atoms.a: allusion
atoms.b: Whenever he tried to invent something, his friends called him ((++Einstein smart)).

wrong.text: There is a reference made to Albert Einstein.

atoms.a: cliché
atoms.b: All that glitters is not ((++gold shimmering)).

wrong.text: This phrase is used to exclaim that not everything that looks precious or true turns out to be so.

atoms.a: exaggeration
verbal irony
atoms.b: As the rain poured down on their picnic, she said, “Oh, that's ((++perfect such_bad)) weather for outdoor fun!”

wrong.text: What is said is the opposite of what is meant.

atoms.a: situational irony
atoms.b: The ((++fire_station school)) burned to the ground last night.

wrong.text: The firefighters working at the fire station usually put out the fire.

atoms.a: dramatic irony
atoms.b: In the horror film, the ((++audience character)) sees the monster hiding in the closet, but the character walks right in.

wrong.text: The audience knows something which the character does not.

atoms.a: juxtaposition
atoms.b: On the same street, a luxury sports car was parked beside a ((++rusty_old_truck a_glistening_limousine)).

wrong.text: The sport car and truck are opposites.

atoms.a: rhetorical question
understatement
atoms.b: After climbing Mount Everest, she said, “It was a ((++bit_cold incredibly_exhausting)).”

wrong.text: The climb is represented as less than it is.

atoms.a: wordplay (pun)
atoms.b: I used to be a baker, but I couldn’t make enough ((++dough money)).

wrong.text: Dough is used as a synonym for money.

instruction.text: Choose which device of style and tone should be used in order to achieve the given goal.

atoms.a: I want to bring something across as extreme.
I want to convey an outcome opposite to what is expected.
I want to highlight the opposition of two items.
I want to use a phrase that is most commonly used.
I want to convey an outcome opposite to what is expected.
I want the audience to know more than the characters.
I purposely want something to come across as less than it is.
I want to make a joke using the literal and figurative meaning of a word.
I do not expect an answer to what I'm asking.
I want to refer to something instead of directly naming it.
